strategy.mode: metadata-first, deterministic, OpenAIRE-aligned export plus richer internal JSON
strategy.title_policy: Single export title only. Multilingual or alternative titles are preserved in internal.title_variants.
strategy.language_policy: dc:language is treated as the resource language. Multilingual metadata literal languages are tracked separately in internal.metadata_languages.
strategy.dates_policy: Export dates are limited to Accepted, Available, Issued. Available falls back to Issued when absent. Submitted, Created and Modified stay in internal.internal_dates.
strategy.alternate_identifier_policy: Internal article IDs are not exported as OpenAIRE alternateIdentifiers; they are preserved only in internal.article_ID/object_ID.
strategy.description_policy: Preserve multilingual DC.Description entries when present.
strategy.files_policy: citation_pdf_url is preferred for oaire:file/fulltext extraction; viewer URLs are deterministically converted to download URLs for internal PDF assets and local PDF saving.
strategy.references_policy: All citation_reference values are preserved as supplemental data; no promotion to OpenAIRE relatedIdentifier.
strategy.warning_diagnostics_policy: If enabled, warnings can trigger an advisory OpenAI call with automatic second attempt and user-controlled further retry loop; AI output is supplemental and never mutates extracted metadata automatically.

title.datacite:title: Toward remote work: Online internship in time of pandemics

descriptions.value: The pandemic deeply affected the curricular internship in higher education since the emergency provisions included mobility limitations and companies’ closure. Since curricular internships are often compulsory for degree attainment, the universities reacted in different ways to ensure the completion of the study programme. This article reports on the collection of data carried out in April-July 2021 in the frame of the ON-IT project about provisions adopted by universities during the worst period of the pandemic emergency. Results are discussed, and the conclusion highlights the next steps of the project development to ensure the quality of online and blended internships to support the acquisition of employability skills for remote work.

The pandemic deeply affected the curricular internship in higher education since the emergency provisions included mobility limitations and companies’ closure. Since curricular internships are often compulsory for degree attainment, the universities reacted in different ways to ensure the completion of the study programme. This article reports on the collection of data carried out in April-July 2021 in the frame of the ON-IT project about provisions adopted by universities during the worst period of the pandemic emergency. Results are discussed, and the conclusion highlights the next steps of the project development to ensure the quality of online and blended internships to support the acquisition of employability skills for remote work.
